moat_against: Regulator caps returns: 9.4% allowed ROE is a ceiling, no pricing power
NY affordability law caps rate-case bill increases below inflation; 2026-28 plan settled far below request
Perpetual external funding dilutes per-share growth (guided EPS CAGR 6-7% vs ~8.7% rate-base growth)
Heavy leverage (net debt $24,172M) and constant refinancing; gas/steam transition risk set by PSC policy
moat_for: Exclusive franchise monopoly for electric/gas/steam delivery in NYC and Westchester — network cannot be replicated
Rate base guided to compound ~8.7%/yr on a ~$38B capital program, capex recovered through rates plus allowed return
52 consecutive years of dividend increases through multiple cycles and regulators
moat_justification: Exclusive regulated electric/gas/steam delivery franchise in NYC and Westchester — no competitor can replicate the network, demand is essential and inelastic, rate base guided to compound ~8.7%/yr on a ~$38B capital program with costs recovered through rates. But the regulator caps the economics: 9.4% allowed ROE at CECONY is a ceiling, NY's affordability law caps rate-case bill increases below inflation, and perpetual debt/equity funding (up to $1.1B new equity in 2026, ~$1.2B in 2027, ~$3.3B in 2028-30) dilutes rate-base growth down to 6-7% guided EPS growth. Durable, but capped — 6/10.
name: Consolidated Edison, Inc.
one_liner: Durable regulated NYC franchise, moat 6/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative 0 of the last 5 years (capex consumes ~all of OCF) — Tier F on this screen; a bond-like ~6-7% guided EPS compounder that does not clear 15% on any reading.
